use /lib
from /scope/lsp import LSP

export scope EditorScope:
    concept: {EditorConcept}

concept EditorConcept:
    pitch:
        An editor for a file opened from the project tree, with language
        support for Piton files.

    shape: {EditorShape}

shape EditorShape:
    description:
        Editable and syntax highlighted, under a header with the file's path
        in the project, a dot while it has unsaved changes, a save button, and
        a close button.

    saving:
        Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on macOS) or the save button writes the file to disk.
        A file that cannot be saved keeps its changes and says why beneath
        the header.

    languageSupport:
        overview:
            A Piton file (`.pi`) is edited with the project's @{LSP} server,
            shared with the chat input, which sees the editor's unsaved text:
            the file is opened with `textDocument/didOpen`, kept current with
            full-text `textDocument/didChange`, reported with
            `textDocument/didSave` when saved, and closed with
            `textDocument/didClose` when the editor closes or shows another
            file. Other files are edited without language support, as is a
            Piton file while the server is not running.

        completions:
            `textDocument/completion` is requested after typing a letter, a
            digit, an opening curly brace, a period, a dollar sign, an at
            sign, a colon, or an underscore, and narrowed and ordered as in
            the chat input. Accepting a completion also applies the import the
            server attaches to it.

        hover:
            Hovering a name shows the server's `textDocument/hover`.

        definitions:
            Ctrl-clicking (Cmd-clicking on macOS) a name goes to its
            `textDocument/definition`. A definition in another file opens that
            file in the editor, at the definition.

        diagnostics:
            What the server publishes for the file is underlined, with the
            message shown on hover, and kept while the text is edited until
            the server publishes again.

        quickFixes:
            Ctrl+. (Cmd+. on macOS) lists the server's
            `textDocument/codeAction` fixes at the cursor, and picking one
            applies its edits to the file.

    replacing:
        Opening another file shows that file in its place. While there are
        unsaved changes, it first asks whether to discard them.

    closing:
        A close button above the file closes it. While there are unsaved
        changes, it first asks whether to discard them.

use /lib
from /scope/harness-integration import HarnessIntegrationScope
from /scope/project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope
from /scope/lsp import LSP

export scope ChatInputScope:
    concept: {ChatInputConcept}

concept ChatInputConcept:
    pitch:
        A multi-line, syntax-highlighted textbox that accepts plain text as well
        as snippets of Piton.

    shape: {ChatInputShape}

shape ChatInputShape:
    description:
        Input on the left, send button on the right.

        <Enter> allows for creating new lines, like Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends it to
        the ${HarnessIntegrationScope}

        Sending is never blocked by the harness working: while it is, the send
        button reads "Queue" and sending adds the prompt to prompt mode's
        queue. The button is only disabled while the input is empty.

    tabs:
        The input and send button live inside the body of a tab bar, using
        gpui-kit's default tab styling. The two tabs are Code and Spec.

        Pressing <Tab> while in the chat input cycles between the tabs, and
        focus remains in the chat input.

    systemPrompt:
        The selected tab is the mode a prompt is sent in, and each mode gives
        the hidden anchor a systemPrompt property alongside its userPrompt.
        The code location is `codeRoot` and the spec location is `root`, as
        set in the project's piton.config.pi.

        code:
            We're working on the code located in <code location>. Don't edit
            the spec located in <spec location>.

        spec:
            We're working on the spec located in <spec location>. Don't edit
            the code located in <code location>.

        A prompt keeps the mode it was sent in while it waits in the queue.

    escape:
        Pressing <Escape> while in the chat input takes focus out of the chat
        input.

    growToFit:
        The text input will grow to fit the text inside of it, one row per
        visual line: both lines broken with <Enter> and long lines that soft
        wrap. It shrinks again as text is removed, and re-fits when the window
        is resized. It starts at a single row, lined up with the send button,
        and stops growing at 12 rows, after which it scrolls.

    autoFocus:
        The chat input should be auto-focused.

    syntaxHighlighting:
        Syntax highlighting will be supported via the [Tree Sitter
        Grammar](https://github.com/piton-lang/tree-sitter-piton)

    lsp: @{LSP}

    harnessMentions:
        overview:
            Typing `/` offers the harness's skills and commands, and typing `@`
            offers its agents, the way they are offered in the harness itself.
            The placeholder mentions both.

        trigger:
            A mention starts at `/` or `@` at the start of the input or after
            whitespace, so paths and email addresses never open it, and an at sign
            followed by an opening curly brace is still a Piton reference. Completions are
            requested after typing the `/` or `@`, and after each letter,
            digit, hyphen, underscore, or colon of the name that follows. Only
            inside a mention are a slash or a hyphen a trigger; outside of one
            they never reach the @{LSP}.

        offered:
            Skills and commands are those of the selected
            ${ProjectDirectoryScope}, of the user, and of the user's enabled
            plugins, a plugin's own being named `plugin:name`. Agents come from
            the same places, plus the harness's built-in agents. Each shows
            whether it is a skill, command, or agent, and its description as
            documentation when it has one. Every harness run reports the skills
            and agents it has, built-in ones included; the last report is saved
            with the project and offered too. Results are narrowed and ordered
            like Piton completions: matches at the start of a name before
            matches anywhere in it, then by name.

        accepting:
            Accepting a skill or command inserts `/name `, and accepting an
            agent inserts `@agent-name `, which the harness understands as a
            request to use that agent. They pass through the hidden anchor and
            its compilation unchanged, so a prompt starting with `/name` runs
            that skill or command. Mentions work without the @{LSP}.

    hiddenAnchor:
        While the user will be able to type plain text, behind the scenes,
        they'll be typing into a randomly-named piton anchor with a userPrompt
        property.  It's this compiled anchor that will be send to the

use /lib
from /scope/harness-integration import HarnessIntegrationScope
from /scope/project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope
from /scope/lsp import LSP

export scope ChatInputScope:
    concept: {ChatInputConcept}

concept ChatInputConcept:
    pitch:
        A multi-line, syntax-highlighted textbox that accepts plain text as well
        as snippets of Piton.

    shape: {ChatInputShape}

shape ChatInputShape:
    description:
        Input on the left, send button on the right.

        <Enter> allows for creating new lines, like Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends it to
        the ${HarnessIntegrationScope}

        Sending is never blocked by the harness working: while it is, the send
        button reads "Queue" and sending adds the prompt to prompt mode's
        queue. The button is only disabled while the input is empty.

    tabs:
        The input and send button live inside the body of a tab bar, using
        gpui-kit's default tab styling. The two tabs are Code and Spec.

        Pressing <Tab> while in the chat input cycles between the tabs, and
        focus remains in the chat input.

    systemPrompt:
        The selected tab is the mode a prompt is sent in, and each mode gives
        the hidden anchor a systemPrompt property alongside its userPrompt.
        The code location is `codeRoot` and the spec location is `root`, as
        set in the project's piton.config.pi.

        code:
            We're working on the code located in <code location>. Don't edit
            the spec located in <spec location>.

        spec:
            We're working on the spec located in <spec location>. Don't edit
            the code located in <code location>.

        A prompt keeps the mode it was sent in while it waits in the queue.

    escape:
        Pressing <Escape> while in the chat input takes focus out of the chat
        input.

    growToFit:
        The text input will grow to fit the text inside of it, one row per
        visual line: both lines broken with <Enter> and long lines that soft
        wrap. It shrinks again as text is removed, and re-fits when the window
        is resized. It starts at a single row, lined up with the send button,
        and stops growing at 12 rows, after which it scrolls.

    autoFocus:
        The chat input should be auto-focused.

    syntaxHighlighting:
        Syntax highlighting will be supported via the [Tree Sitter
        Grammar](https://github.com/piton-lang/tree-sitter-piton)

    lsp: @{LSP}

    harnessMentions:
        overview:
            Typing `/` offers the harness's skills and commands, and typing `@`
            offers its agents, the way they are offered in the harness itself.
            The placeholder mentions both.

        trigger:
            A mention starts at `/` or `@` at the start of the input or after
            whitespace, so paths and email addresses never open it, and an at sign
            followed by an opening curly brace is still a Piton reference. Completions are
            requested after typing the `/` or `@`, and after each letter,
            digit, hyphen, underscore, or colon of the name that follows. Only
            inside a mention are a slash or a hyphen a trigger; outside of one
            they never reach the @{LSP}.

        offered:
            Skills and commands are those of the selected
            ${ProjectDirectoryScope}, of the user, and of the user's enabled
            plugins, a plugin's own being named `plugin:name`. Agents come from
            the same places, plus the harness's built-in agents. Each shows
            whether it is a skill, command, or agent, and its description as
            documentation when it has one. Every harness run reports the skills
            and agents it has, built-in ones included; the last report is saved
            with the project and offered too. Results are narrowed and ordered
            like Piton completions: matches at the start of a name before
            matches anywhere in it, then by name.

        accepting:
            Accepting a skill or command inserts `/name `, and accepting an
            agent inserts `@agent-name `, which the harness understands as a
            request to use that agent. They pass through the hidden anchor and
            its compilation unchanged, so a prompt starting with `/name` runs
            that skill or command. Mentions work without the @{LSP}.

    hiddenAnchor:
        While the user will be able to type plain text, behind the scenes,
        they'll be typing into a randomly-named piton anchor with a userPrompt
        property.  It's this compiled anchor that will be send to the
        @{HarnessIntegrationScope}

            they never reach the @{LSP}.

        offered:
            Skills and commands are those of the selected
            ${ProjectDirectoryScope}, of the user, and of the user's enabled
            plugins, a plugin's own being named `plugin:name`. Agents come from
            the same places, plus the harness's built-in agents. Each shows
            whether it is a skill, command, or agent, and its description as
            documentation when it has one. Every harness run reports the skills
            and agents it has, built-in ones included; the last report is saved
            with the project and offered too. Results are narrowed and ordered
            like Piton completions: matches at the start of a name before
            matches anywhere in it, then by name.

        accepting:
            Accepting a skill or command inserts `/name `, and accepting an
            agent inserts `@agent-name `, which the harness understands as a
            request to use that agent. They pass through the hidden anchor and
            its compilation unchanged, so a prompt starting with `/name` runs
            that skill or command. Mentions work without the @{LSP}.

    hiddenAnchor:
        While the user will be able to type plain text, behind the scenes,
        they'll be typing into a randomly-named piton anchor with a userPrompt
        property.  It's this compiled anchor that will be send to the
        @{HarnessIntegrationScope}

content.text:
I updated the chat input spec in `spec/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.pi`, and `piton check` passes. I didn't touch `./src`.

The spec had never described the chain button at all, only the Code and Spec tabs. So I wrote the button up as it works in the code today, then added your changes:

- **Tabs:** there are now three stops. The chain sits between Code and Spec and selects both (its tooltip reads "Code and Spec"). `<Tab>` goes Code → chain → Spec → Code, and `<Shift+Tab>` goes the other way.
- **No focus border:** the chain is a small square, half the height of the tabs and centred on them, with no focus border.
- **Off:** it shows a broken chain at 50% opacity. Code and Spec sit apart with a gap wide enough that the chain fits between them without overlapping either tab.
- **On:** it shows a joined chain at full opacity and both tabs are selected. The tabs slide together until they meet under the chain, which covers the join so they look like one locked tab. Turning it off slides them apart again.
- **The chain never moves:** it stays in the same place in both states; only the tabs slide.

I also added a `both` entry to the system prompts, matching the code: "We're working on both the code located in … and the spec located in …. Edit both of them."

The code doesn't match the new spec yet. Right now the chain always overlaps the tabs, and a test (`chain_tab_overlaps_the_tabs`) checks for that overlap even when the chain is off, so that test will need to change when the code is updated.
